taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Vernonia lindheimeri; native range includes Texas.
look_here_first: Narrow-leaved purple ironweed of dry rocky sites: linear leaves with densely woolly lower surfaces, usually glabrate upper surfaces, and strongly revolute margins.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis and Kerr are exact target-zone records. Williamson is documented but outside the project target-county list and is not counted.

approval_exception.reason: Correct stale PASS while preserving learner admission.

best_field_traits: purple discoid heads in corymbiform arrays
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Much narrower-leaved than V. baldwinii; watch for intermediate V. × guadalupensis.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Linear revolute leaves with woolly undersides strongly favor V. lindheimeri; intermediates may be hybrid.

visual_learning.learner_goal: Recognize V. lindheimeri as the narrow, strongly revolute, woolly-underleaf parent endpoint and distinguish it from broad-leaved V. baldwinii without forcing intermediate hybrids.

verified_measurement_anchor.teaching_use: Photograph a mature mid-stem leaf beside a scale so the extremely narrow proportion is visually obvious.

look_sequence.look_at: one mature cauline leaf with scale
look_sequence.question: Is the blade truly linear and only a few millimeters wide?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Use the reviewed cauline-leaf range of about 5–8 cm × 2–4 mm as a visual anchor, not flower color.

look_sequence.question: Are the margins strongly rolled under (revolute)?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Side lighting or a small cross-section diagram makes the rolled margin much easier to learn than a flat photo.

look_sequence.question: Is the underside densely sericeo-tomentose/woolly?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Use a macro with an arrow to the dense pale hairs.

look_sequence.question: Is the upper surface comparatively glabrate?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Pair upper and lower macros from the same leaf so the contrast is learned directly.

look_sequence.look_at: same characters on possible V. baldwinii or hybrid material
look_sequence.question: Does the plant sit cleanly at this narrow/revolute/woolly endpoint?
look_sequence.teaching_note: Intermediate leaf width, margin roll or indumentum should trigger V. × guadalupensis rather than a forced parent ID.

same_frame_features: whole mature leaf at same scale
comparison_board.lindheimeri_side: linear cauline leaf about 5–8 cm × 2–4 mm; strongly revolute margin; densely woolly lower surface; upper surface usually glabrate
comparison_board.other_side: much broader ovate to lance-ovate leaf; lower surface hairy/tomentose
comparison_board.best_visual_lock: same-scale leaf + margin profile + paired upper/lower surface macros

comparison_board.other_side: natural hybrid may bridge V. lindheimeri and V. baldwinii

photo_diagram_needs.annotation: label reviewed 5–8 cm × 2–4 mm range and mark width axis
arrows showing both margins rolled under; optional simple cross-section inset
label usually glabrate upper surface versus densely sericeo-tomentose lower surface

photo_diagram_needs.role: three-column V. baldwinii × V. guadalupensis V. lindheimeri comparison
photo_diagram_needs.annotation: same scale and same diagnostic views for all three

photo_diagram_needs.annotation: connect habit view to the leaf sampled for the diagnostic close-ups

avoid_overtrusting: one leaf on an intermediate plant
range status as an identification character
